Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The failing test `testLang538` attempts to format a `GregorianCalendar` constructed with the time zone "GMT-8". The expected formatted date string is an ISO8601 date-time string in UTC ("Zulu") time zone: "2009-10-16T16:42:16.000Z".

Looking into the formatting code in `FastDateFormat`, the key method is `format(Calendar)`, which calls `format(Calendar, StringBuffer)`. In that method, if `mTimeZoneForced` is true, the calendar is cloned and its time zone is set to the formatter's time zone (UTC in this test). Then the formatting rules are applied.

The bug report mentions that in certain situations, setting the time zone of a `Calendar` using `setTimeZone` does not correctly update its fields unless a `getTime()` call is made on the calendar first (a known JDK quirk). Because `FastDateFormat.format` sets the calendar time zone but apparently does not call `getTime()` after that, the calendar fields used for formatting are stale or incorrect. This causes the formatted time to not reflect the expected time zone conversion, making the test fail.

The recent bug reports do not provide additional info on this. The main code snippet shows that `format` clones the calendar and sets its time zone but performs no call to fix fields by accessing `getTime()`.

Hence, the root cause is that after forcing the time zone on the cloned calendar inside `format(Calendar, StringBuffer)`, the calendar's internal fields are not synchronized with its instant because no call like `getTime()` is made to force field recalculation. This results in wrong formatting output when the original calendar was constructed in certain time zones or ways that trigger the JDK issue.

A fix would be for `FastDateFormat.format` to call `calendar.getTime()` after `calendar.setTimeZone(mTimeZone)` to force the calendar to update its fields before formatting. This would ensure the time conversion is applied properly and the formatted output matches expectations.

In summary, the bug stems from JDK's `Calendar` behavior combined with the lack of defensive code in `FastDateFormat.format(Calendar)` to fix this by forcing field recalculation after changing the calendar's time zone.

Recommended fix location:
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.time.FastDateFormat.format(java.util.Calendar,java.lang.StringBuffer)`

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
